I'm somewhat conflicted on what to do about docs#Ordinal.IsFundamentalSequence. On the one hand, the notion of fundamental sequences for ordinal appears quite often in the relevant literature. But on the other hand... I don't think it's a very useful notion? It just boils down to just choosing a cofinal subset of minimum order type (see docs#Ordinal.ord_cof_eq) and enumerating it.

We currently use this to prove some basic results about cofinalities, such as cof (cof x) = cof x and cof (f a) = cof a for normal f, but #36702 and #36703 make it so that this is no longer the case (and the new proofs are nicer, in my view). So, should we perhaps remove fundamental sequences entirely?

@Snir Broshi @Bhavik Mehta

I guess my question is: why is "I don't find it very useful" a reason to remove something that's already in Mathlib? I wouldn't be surprised if Mathlib has a lot of not-very-useful lemmas... is the concern that the library is getting too bloated and needs to be trimmed down?

There is another issue with docs#Ordinal.IsFundamentalSequence. It's defined in terms of docs#Ordinal.blsub, which is just a special case of docs#iSup with its own bespoke API. I've been trying to get rid of it for quite a while, and this is in the way of that.
Ahh, I see. I'm guessing it would be a hassle to rewrite IsFundamentalSeq to use iSup?
hence your debate about whether or not it's worth keeping in the first place
It's work that can be avoided if I just deprecate it :slight_smile:

Elaborating a bit more on why I think it's unnecessary. What docs#Ordinal.exists_fundamental_sequence tells you is that there exists some dependent function which enumerates the elements of some cofinal subset for a given ordinal with minimal order type. But docs#Ordinal.ord_cof_eq accomplishes the same without having to go through blsub/iSup, and without the dependent typing.
I ultimately decided against getting rid of fundamental sequences. Instead I re-defined them so as to avoid the dependent types and the use of blsub. #37019
